explain.say: Imagine packing for a trip round the Solar System. On one world you could jump over a bus; on another you could barely stand up. Your body would not change at all. So what does? Your weight! Let us compare.

faq.q: Why do you weigh less on the Moon?
faq.a: The Moon has much less mass than Earth, so its gravity is weaker, about one sixth as strong.
asks: What would I weigh on the Moon?

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter in you, in kilograms, and is the same everywhere. Weight is the force of gravity on you, in newtons.

faq.q: Why would you weigh so much on Jupiter?
faq.a: Jupiter is enormous, more than 300 times Earth's mass, so its gravitational pull at the cloud tops is about two and a half times Earth's.
asks: Why is gravity strong on Jupiter?

faq.a: Weight equals mass times gravitational field strength. On Earth that is about 9.8 newtons per kilogram.

faq.q: Does your mass change in space?
faq.a: No. Your mass stays the same everywhere. Only your weight changes with the strength of gravity.
asks: Is mass the same on the Moon?

facts: Gravitational field strength is about 9.8 N/kg on Earth, 1.6 N/kg on the Moon and 24.8 N/kg on Jupiter.

quiz.say: An astronaut has a mass of 70 kg on Earth. What is their mass on the Moon?
quiz.show: An astronaut has a mass of 70 kg on Earth. What is their mass on the Moon?
quiz.why: Mass is the same everywhere; only weight changes.

wrong.0: That is roughly one sixth; weight changes but mass does not.
wrong.1: Mass never disappears; it is the amount of matter.

quiz.why: Weight is a force, and forces are measured in newtons.
